title: You are here

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: When you look at the commit graph, how does git know where you are?

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: It uses a special label called HEAD.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: HEAD always points to the commit you are currently looking at in your working folder.

questions.prompt: Run `git log --oneline`. What commit is HEAD pointing to?
questions.explanation: Right now, HEAD is pointing to the latest commit. It is your "You are here" marker.

hints: Run `git log --oneline` and look at the first line.
You will see `(HEAD -> main)` next to the latest commit.
recap: HEAD is a pointer that tells git where you are in the history. It usually points to the newest commit.
